condition: progressive frontal hairline recession with perifollicular scaling over 10 months in a Black woman wearing braided hairstyles
level_rationale: Ten months of progressive frontal hairline recession accompanied by flaking around the hair follicles in a 36-year-old Black woman wearing braided hairstyles raises concern for scarring frontal fibrosing or chronic traction hair loss requiring dermatologist trichoscopy and anti-inflammatory therapy before permanent follicular destruction occurs, whereas feeling mild front hairline tightness for 1 hour right after braiding reflects benign temporary styling tension manageable with self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (36-year-old Black woman, 10 months of braided hair, and progressive front hairline recession with root flaking) with zero apostrophe contractions ('Im', 'I am', 'has'), zero diagnosis labels ('alopecia' omitted), a 2-word span difference (18 vs 20 words), and orthogonal 2x2 crossing. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 on the exact same front hairline to 1 hour of mild post-braiding tightness leaves zero stranded hair loss or scaling while shifting care cleanly from dermatologist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
